operator_request: Implement WP-FF-008 with no more than three parallel subagents, independent multi-lens adversarial review of every large block, long-wait tolerance, no interference with unrelated processes, final artifact cleanup, and no yt-dlp dependency anywhere in Ferric.
spec_anchors: Section 23 persistence, resume, staged commit, and crash reconciliation
assumptions: A single Ferric process owns one archive database; concurrent claims are concurrent tasks/threads, not multi-process writers.
Only reconciled committed outputs become archive successes.
The adapter may serialize writes while permitting concurrent reads if the candidate contract requires it.
Filesystem crash/power-loss proof remains bounded by WP-009 capability profiles and must not be overclaimed.
non_goals: No SQLite or other native dependency approval.
No production feature, runtime, package, release, or phase completion claim.
No Python, yt-dlp, yt-dlp companion asset, executable, subprocess, fallback, sidecar, plugin, service, or delegated dependency.
No backend-specific identity semantics in public contracts.

research_basis.method: Current official repository, release, manifest, design, changelog, test, issue-surface, benchmark, and RustSec source inspection; exact release tags were shallow-cloned under ignored .fforager-artifacts/research for source-level review.

checked: no package advisory entry found for redb, fjall, or sled

patterns_found: redb 4.1.0 is maintained, pure Rust, ACID, MVCC, stable-format, crash-repairing, and has no mandatory normal dependency with default features disabled.
redb's default one-fsync checksum commit has a documented hostile-input theoretical ceiling; Ferric must select two-phase durability for archive commits and test that setting.
redb 4.0/4.1 fixed data-loss, corruption, savepoint, and transaction defects, so exact pinning plus Ferric boundary fault tests are mandatory.
fjall 3.1.8 is maintained and pure Rust but default writes reach OS buffers until explicit PersistMode::SyncAll; it carries a broader normal dependency surface and background maintenance.
sled 0.34.7 has an old release line, extensive unsafe code, and a broader legacy dependency surface; it is unsuitable as the first candidate.
Candidate semantics must remain behind Ferric-owned identities and archive state transitions so a later candidate reruns the same workload.

selected_approach.durability_profile: two-phase immediate durability for archive commits
selected_approach.reason: Smallest maintained pure-Rust transactional candidate matching single-process archive ownership, crash recovery, stable format, range lookup, and concurrent-reader needs with the narrowest dependency graph inspected.

rejected_or_deferred.reason: Would reinvent transactions, indexing, repair, and migrations without field hardening.
Viable maintained pure-Rust LSM candidate, but explicit persistence, background maintenance, and broader dependencies add proof surface for Ferric's archive workload.
Stale release line, extensive unsafe implementation surface, and legacy dependencies increase maintenance and correctness risk.
Native binding/runtime dependency remains outside the Operator-approved boundary and cannot be pre-approved by this spike.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: A database commit and output filesystem state diverge.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Keep staged-output reconciliation authoritative, archive only reconciled output identities, and inject both row-without-output and output-without-row.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Concurrent claim or lease takeover creates duplicates.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Use one atomic write transaction with versioned lease tokens and deterministic stale/fresh clocks; test races and stale-token rejection.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Candidate corruption or migration interruption is misreported as success.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Fail closed with typed errors, keep migration state/version records, preserve last-known-good source, and execute interrupted/corrupt cases.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Million-identity scale loads all keys into memory.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Stream deterministic generation/insertion, bound batches/cache, record RSS and database size, and reject evidence missing resource observations.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: The candidate's self-claims replace Ferric proof.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Run behavior-sensitive public-boundary counterfactuals and validate observed state independently from expected labels.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: yt-dlp enters through fixtures or delegated tooling.
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Use only committed Ferric-owned corpus data and enforce dependency/source/asset negative fixtures; canonical verification succeeds with yt-dlp absent.

validation_plan: Contract schema strictness and identity collision/alias fixtures.
Public candidate-neutral claim, lease, success insertion, membership, and reconciliation tests.
Concurrent duplicate claims and deterministic stale lease takeover.
Corrupt/torn store, row/output mismatch, interrupted migration, and unknown import mapping refusal.
Representative and one-million-identity controlled runs with timeout, latency distributions, RSS, file size, and write amplification proxy.
Dependency graph, features, sources, licenses, build scripts, native links, unsafe source, and yt-dlp/Python prohibition checks.
Independent multi-lens adversarial reviews followed by remediation regressions and full rerun.

execution_decomposition.scope: identity, provenance, claim/lease, insertion, reconciliation, migration/import DTOs, bounds, typed errors
candidate-neutral boundary and exact-pinned redb adapter with two-phase immediate durability
fixtures, deterministic faults/concurrency/scale workloads, xtask report and gate integration, model manual

red_team.attack: race two workers for one asset then expire and reuse a lease
red_team.minimum_control: one winner, exact token ownership, stale/fresh clock boundary, old-token commit rejection

red_team.attack: crash or corrupt every archive/migration/reconciliation prefix
red_team.minimum_control: idempotent declared recovery or typed fail-closed result with no false success

red_team.attack: substitute expected labels, reports, or fixture inventories for behavior
red_team.minimum_control: public producer-consumer observations and declaration-preserving behavior mutations

red_team.attack: make the scale run pass by loading everything into memory or skipping B-021
red_team.minimum_control: streaming workload, explicit resource observations, timeout, and blocked-not-pass handling
negative fixtures for wrappers/assets plus canonical dependency/source scan
